stresses: TWO real, current, fully-independent HVAC systems -- a furnace (manufacturer/model/fuel-question/year) and a separately-standalone-duct central AC (its own attic ducts, insulation, leakage) -- explicitly NOT sharing ducts, with identity detail belonging to one and duct detail belonging to the other. Under the old single-instance format this was UNREPRESENTABLE and the file recorded the loss; the instance format now expresses it, which makes this transcript the corpus's primary ATTRIBUTION test: a run can emit the right number of systems and still put the furnace's identity and the AC's ducts on one record. Also: THE named silent-drop trap -- equipment is unambiguous (furnace) but the auditor explicitly declines the fuel ('I can't tell you the fuel on this one') and this must land as declared_absent, not collapse to the same 'unmentioned' a never-discussed fuel would get. Two more declared absences stack alongside (model year unreadable; attic depth explicitly not measured, only the R-value eyeballed). A genuine partial value ('model G-something') that is incomplete but still a real, stated fragment. A clean wall-insulation call ('some, but poor' -> 'Poorly').

arguable.note: The auditor states a genuine partial reading ('model G-something') rather than declining outright -- a real, if incomplete, fragment, analogous to a stated R-value being a real independent value even when a depth is also unmeasured. Asserted verbatim rather than declared_absent, since something concrete WAS read off the plate ('G-...'), unlike the model year (below), where nothing at all was legible. It is explicitly incomplete ('I couldn't get the full model number off the corner it was jammed into'), so a model that leaves this null instead of inventing digits is a defensible caution, not a penalized miss.

notes.instances.hvac: THE LOSS NOTE THIS FILE USED TO CARRY IS RESOLVED, and that resolution is the point of R1.6. Previously both systems shared one hvac record: the equipment-type/manufacturer/model/fuel/year cluster described the FURNACE while hvacDuctLocation/hvacDuctLeakage/hvacDuctInsulation described the AC's attic ductwork, so the record asserted something false about a real appliance and no encoding of it could recover 'both systems, correctly attributed'. They are now two instances and each field sits on the system it belongs to. What this file now tests is whether extraction reproduces that split: emitting TWO hvac instances is necessary but not sufficient, because a run can get the count right and still mix the clusters. The attribution metric, not the enumeration metric, is what this transcript grades.
notes.instances.hvac[1].hvacSystemEquipmentTyp: The AC's own equipment type comes from 'Central AC, standalone ducts', stated separately from the furnace's line. The furnace instance's equipment type no longer carries an `arguable` alternative: the alternative it listed WAS this instance, so once both exist the choice is not a judgement call.
notes._general: No blanket negation appears anywhere in this transcript, so `disclaimers` is empty -- window, dhw, health and basedata are never brought up and correctly resolve to 'unmentioned'. The 'no wait' self-correction in paragraph 2 ('up in the attic there's an air handler, no wait, the furnace itself is in the closet and the AC air handler's the separate thing') is an INSTANCE-LEVEL correction: it does not retract a leaf value, it clarifies that the air handler and the furnace are different machines -- which is precisely the distinction the two instances below encode. wall.wallCavityInsulation (an R-value) stays unmentioned on purpose: 'a couple inches of old batt' states a thickness, and walls have no depth leaf.
